name: Raclopride
summary: Raclopride is a typical antipsychotic. It acts as a selective antagonist on D2 dopamine receptors. It has been used in trials studying Parkinson Disease.

pharmacology.text: It acts as a selective antagonist on D2 dopamine receptors. Raclopride is selective for D2 and D3 dopamine receptors. Images obtained by cerebral PET scanning (e.g. PET/CT or PET/MRI) allow the non-invasive assessment of the binding capacity of the cerebral D2 dopamine receptor, which can be useful for the diagnosis of movement disorders.

uses.text: It has been used in trials studying Parkinson Disease. It can be radiolabelled with radioisotopes, e.g. 3H or 11C and used as a tracer for in vitro imaging (autoradiography) as well as in vivo imaging positron emission tomography (PET). Radiolabelled raclopride is also commonly used to determine the efficacy and neurotoxicity of dopaminergic drugs.

fact.en: Raclopride labelled with radioactive carbon is widely used in PET brain scans to measure how many dopamine D2 receptors are free, which is how researchers watch dopamine release in the living brain.
fact.zh: 以放射性碳標記的 raclopride 被廣泛用於 PET 腦部掃描，測量有多少多巴胺 D2 受體處於空閒狀態，研究人員藉此觀察活體腦中的多巴胺釋放。
fact.zhHans: 以放射性碳标记的 raclopride 被广泛用于 PET 脑部扫描，测量有多少多巴胺 D2 受体处于空闲状态，研究人员借此观察活体脑中的多巴胺释放。
